title: Approval loop UX: keyboard-first approval card with redirect, persisted site rules and attention notifications
summary: Extend the existing browser approval gate into a full loop. Model Plane owns the approval schema (risk level, display-friendly params, origin, page URL, persist session|always) and persisted per-user or per-org host rules stored as BrowserBroker policy, never widened through Spaces. The SPA renders a keyboard-first card in chat and in the browser panel (Allow with Mod+Enter, Deny with Esc, and a 'do this instead' text that is delivered to the planner as a redirect, plus 'do not ask again' for non-sensitive categories) and deep-links denials to the setting that caused them. Application Plane emits notifications for approval_requested, question and completed with a link into the run, and suppresses them while the session is visible.
whyItMatters: The risk categories and the fail-closed deterministic check are already good; what users feel is a card that only approves or rejects, cannot be answered outside the browser panel, and repeats the same question. Background runs need a reliable way to pull the user back without noise, and 'always' rules cut approval fatigue without widening any ACL.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (approval contract, automation-and-safety-064) for the schema; Aside (aside-agent-control-architecture-076) for the card UX; Aside (aside-agent-control-architecture-059, aside-browser-product-097) for visibility-aware notifications

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Approval prompts: 2 of 3 sources, common. Attention notifications: 2 of 3, common.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Approval request = {kind, connector, tool, params_display[{name, display_name, value}], riskLevel low|high, persist ['session','always'], origin, page_url}. UI choices: Allow, Deny, free text that rejects with 'user asked to do X instead', and 'always' that writes a site rule; denials carry a deep link to the permission setting. Notifications: the UI reports {surfaceId, focused, visible, engaged, sessionId, sequence} on focus changes plus a heartbeat; the backend keeps per-user attention entries with 30 and 60 second TTLs and skips notifying for visible sessions, disabled settings and ephemeral sessions; blocking asks use requireInteraction and open the session on click.

verevonToday.gap: Missing: session/always persistence tied to broker host rules, redirect-with-instruction, keyboard shortcuts, display-friendly params, resolving an approval outside the browser panel, settings deep links, and browser-run notification events with visibility suppression. Also unreachable end to end until grants are issued (R-t2-08-01).

approach: Model Plane: extend the approval record and the planner reply path with params_display, persist and redirect_text; persist 'always' as BrowserBroker policy rules keyed by (user or org, host, category) and keep upload/download/dialog single-use. Frontend Plane: shared approval card used in chat and the browser panel, keyboard shortcuts, settings deep links, and a visibility heartbeat. Application Plane: browser event types on the existing notifications API with cta_href to the run; ZDR or ephemeral sessions send title-only bodies.
planeOwner: Model Plane (schema and rules) with Frontend Plane and Application Plane
risks: Over-broad 'always' rules (keep sensitive categories single-use); notification bodies must not leak page content under ZDR; the notification half is unverified.

verevon.exactGap: Shipped: the Phase 5 per-action HITL gate for the durable browser-agent loop (deterministic classify_action_risk categories, fail-closed require_approval on the durable Approval record, BrowserApprovalCard with Bokmal risk labels, decisions through the orchestration approvals API with an optional decision reason). Confirmed missing: keyboard shortcuts (the card is click-only), redirect-with-instruction (a denial aborts the whole run by design in gate_risky_action and the reason only appears in the abort text), session/always persistence and persisted site rules (broker grants are in-memory and per-grant, and capability-core policy rejects user scope), display-friendly params beyond reason, url and selector, and any approval_requested or question notification or visibility suppression (notification-core authorizes only capability-core's run_completed and run_failed, and insight-core consumes approval events for metrics only). The item also understates duplication and the chat gap: chat has a separate ApprovalRequests deck (approve and reject only), and agent-loop approvals are created by pause_for_approval with a generic reason such as tool 'browser.act' requires approval and no risk category, so the richer card exists only for the browser panel's durable runs.

verevon.constraints: Persisted 'always' rules cannot live as BrowserBroker policy: broker grants are in-memory and per-grant. The owner-plane home is capability-core's policy engine, which today supports only org and global scope (IsSupportedScope rejects user), so per-user always-allow needs a trusted user binding first and Space membership must never widen a rule. Model proposes, Quarry executes: redirect text is a user-authored instruction and the next proposed action must pass the same deterministic classifier and Quarry grant checks; abort-on-deny is a deliberate fail-closed choice, so changing it is a behavior change needing tests. Sensitive categories (login, checkout, destructive, upload, download, dialog) stay single-use. ZDR: notification bodies title-only, no page text or URL. Notifications originate in the Model Plane (capability-core) and are delivered by Application Plane notification-core, not emitted by Application Plane itself. Escape is already globally bound, so Esc=Deny needs collision review.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reorder into independently shippable slices. (1) Frontend only: one shared approval card for chat and the browser panel, keyboard shortcuts through the existing shortcut hook, redirect text sent in the existing decision reason. (2) Model Plane: enrich approval creation on the agent-loop path (pause_for_approval) with params_display and risk category, and let the planner receive redirect text as a user message after a denial instead of aborting. (3) Org-level persisted rules in capability-core policy, not BrowserBroker; per-user only after a user-scope binding exists. (4) An approval_requested notification type added to the capability-core runwatch path and the notification-core allowlist, with visibility suppression via a presence heartbeat as a later step.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged as one item, but it spans SPA, Model Plane, capability-core and notification-core; slice (1) is S to M and slices (3) and (4) are each M.
verevon.verdictReason: Status and gap are largely right, but the rule store belongs in capability-core policy rather than BrowserBroker, notifications originate in the Model Plane, the chat approval path is weaker than the item says, and the redirect needs a deliberate change to abort-on-deny. Reword and slice.
